definition: סַד noun [masculine] stocks , for confining feet of culprits (probably loan-word from Aramaic סַדָּא , סַדָּנָא ; Late Hebrew סַד , plural סַדִּין ); = Latin nervus , Greek ποδοκάκη ; — absolute רַגְלַיִם ׳ שִׂים בַּמּ Job 13:27 ( ᵐ5 κώλύμα ), Job 33:11 ( ᵑ6 ξύλό ); (compare synonym מַהְפֶּכֶת , and Greek equivalent there cited).

סַד noun [masculine] stocks, for confining feet of culprits (probably loan-word from Aramaic סַדָּא, סַדָּנָא ; Late Hebrew סַד, plural סַדִּין); = Latin nervus, Greek ποδοκάκη; — absolute רַגְלַיִם׳שִׂים בַּמּ Job 13:27 (ᵐ5 κώλύμα), Job 33:11 (ᵑ6 ξύλό); (compare synonym מַהְפֶּכֶת, and Greek equivalent there cited).
